results.claim: One round has the exact form T(p)=reverse(p_i : i in D) followed by (p_i : i not in D), where D={i>=2 : p_i<p_{i-1}} and both subsequences otherwise retain index order.
results.proof_sketch: The marked elements are precisely the descent bottoms indexed by D. They are moved to the front in increasing index order. Each new move precedes all earlier moves, so their final order is decreasing index order. Removing and moving them does not change the relative order of unmarked elements.

results.claim: There is an exact reduction of every maximum-element phase to parallel deletion in a word. Once i+1,...,n are fixed, write the active prefix as L i R. Define A(r_1...r_s)=(r_j : 2<=j<=s and r_{j-1}<r_j). The number of further rounds until i is fixed is h(R)=min{t:A^t(R) is empty}.
results.proof_sketch: Element i is never marked. The first element of R is marked because it is smaller than i; a later r_j is marked exactly when r_j<r_{j-1}. Thus the elements remaining to the right of i after the round are exactly A(R), independently of L. Iteration proves the formula. Moreover h is computable in one scan: start a stack with sentinel +infinity. For each x, pop while the top value is smaller than x, let tau(x)=1 plus the largest tau among popped entries (zero if none), and push (x,tau(x)). The stack remains decreasing in value, and induction on the scan shows tau(x) is exactly x's deletion round. Hence h=max tau.

results.claim: Let B_0 be empty and B_{m+1}=(m+1)T(B_m). If q(m)=floor((sqrt(8m+1)-1)/2), then h(B_m)=q(m). For m>=2, B_m begins with m and the word to its right also has extinction time q(m).
results.proof_sketch: Apply the labeled monotone stack from the phase reduction. Writing m=q(q+1)/2+r with 0<=r<=q, a simultaneous induction on m gives the following stronger invariant for the final decreasing stack: its values are consecutive, and its labels are (1,q,q-1,...,q-r,q-r-2,...,1) when r<=q-2, and (1,q,q-1,...,1) when r=q-1 or q, with empty ranges omitted. Thus its maximum label is q, proving h(B_m)=q. By definition B_m=mR_m. Since m exceeds every entry of R_m, A(B_m)=A(R_m). For m>=2 both words are nonempty, so h(B_m)=1+h(A(B_m))=1+h(A(R_m))=h(R_m).

results.claim: For i>=2, a phase for active maximum i has its maximum possible length i-1 if and only if its active prefix is exactly (i,1,2,...,i-1).
results.proof_sketch: Write the prefix as L i R. The phase length is h(R)<=|R|<=i-1. Equality forces |R|=i-1, hence L is empty, and also h(R)=|R|. Because A always deletes its first entry, extinction can take |R| rounds only if the first application deletes exactly one entry. Thus every adjacent pair of R is increasing. Since R contains all values 1,...,i-1, it is exactly (1,2,...,i-1). Conversely, for this increasing word, each application of A deletes only its first entry, so h(R)=i-1.

results.claim: If ell_i denotes the phase length for active maximum i, then ell_i+ell_{i-1}<=2i-4 for every i>=5.
results.proof_sketch: Always ell_{i-1}<=i-2. If ell_i<=i-2, the result follows immediately. Otherwise ell_i=i-1, so the rigidity claim makes the phase start (i,1,...,i-1). Induction using the round formula gives T^t(i,1,...,i-1)=B_t,i,t+1,...,i-1 for 0<=t<=i-1. Hence its endpoint is B_{i-1},i. The next phase therefore has length q(i-1). For i>=5, q(i-1)<=i-3: otherwise q>=i-2 would imply (i-2)(i-1)/2<=i-1 and hence i<=4. Thus ell_i+ell_{i-1}<=(i-1)+(i-3)=2i-4.

results.claim: For n>=5, W(n)<=n(n-1)/2-floor((n-3)/2). Consequently no permutation family requires omega(n^2) rounds.
results.proof_sketch: The individual bounds ell_i<=i-1 sum to n(n-1)/2. Group the phases into the disjoint adjacent pairs (n,n-1),(n-2,n-3), and so on, stopping when the larger index is below 5. There are floor((n-3)/2) such pairs. For a pair headed by i, the separate caps sum to (i-1)+(i-2)=2i-3, whereas the preceding obstruction gives at most 2i-4. Each pair therefore saves at least one round, proving the displayed bound. Division by n^2 still gives a bounded ratio, ruling out little-omega(n^2).

results.claim: A substantially stronger uniform adjacent-pair bound ell_i+ell_{i-1}<=i+1 is false: for (7,1,2,3,4,5,6), the phases for 7 and 6 have lengths 6 and 3, respectively.
results.proof_sketch: The special-state identity gives six rounds until 7 fixes, leaving B_6,7. The B-word extinction formula gives q(6)=3 for the phase of 6. Hence the adjacent sum is 9, while i+1=8. This exact boundary counterexample prevents using that tempting stronger pair estimate without additional hypotheses.

results.claim: For p_n=(n,1,2,...,n-1) and n>=3, at least n-1+floor((sqrt(8(n-1)+1)-1)/2) rounds are required.
results.proof_sketch: The identity T^t(p_n)=B_t,n,t+1,...,n-1 for 0<=t<=n-1 shows that n first fixes after n-1 rounds, leaving B_{n-1},n. The next active maximum is n-1. By the B-word extinction formula, its right word has extinction time q(n-1)=floor((sqrt(8(n-1)+1)-1)/2). These two completed phases already require the claimed number of rounds.

results.claim: Under the zero-no-op-round convention, the exact worst-case values for n=1,...,9 are 0,1,3,6,9,12,18,21,26.
results.proof_sketch: Exhaustive enumeration evaluated every permutation using the exact round map above. For n=2,...,8, (n,1,...,n-1) attains the listed maximum. For n=9, (3,9,4,5,1,2,6,7,8) attains 26 rounds. Exhaustion supplies the matching upper bounds.

final_writeup:
Let W(n) be the maximum number of genuine transformations before the identity is reached. One round moves precisely the descent bottoms to the front in reverse index order. This yields an exact phase description: once all values larger than i are fixed, write the active prefix as L i R. The word remaining to the right of i after one round is A(R), where A retains exactly the ascent tops. Hence the phase length is the extinction time h(R).

The obstruction analysis gives a new restriction on consecutive phases. A phase for i can attain its individual maximum i-1 only in the unique state (i,1,2,...,i-1). That phase ends in B_{i-1},i, where B_0 is empty and B_{m+1}=(m+1)T(B_m). The labeled monotone-stack invariant gives h(B_m)=floor((sqrt(8m+1)-1)/2), and the tail following the leading m has the same height. Thus, after a maximally long phase for i, the next phase has only this triangular-root length. Combining this exceptional case with the ordinary individual bounds proves

W(n) <= n(n-1)/2 - floor((n-3)/2)  for n>=5.

In particular, the singled-out superquadratic possibility is impossible: no permutation family requires omega(n^2) rounds. The obstruction has a real limitation. For (7,1,2,3,4,5,6), the first two phase lengths are 6 and 3, so the tempting stronger bound ell_i+ell_{i-1}<=i+1 already fails at i=7.

The retained explicit lower-bound family p_n=(n,1,2,...,n-1) requires n-1 rounds to fix n and then floor((sqrt(8(n-1)+1)-1)/2) further rounds to fix n-1. Exact enumeration gives W(1),...,W(9)=0,1,3,6,9,12,18,21,26.
